title: Potatoism Timeline and Story Arc
epistemic_rule: This timeline mixes project-canon mythology with explicitly labelled comparative or symbolic material. It is not a factual biography of a supernatural being. Dates supplied by the project are preserved as claims and should be distinguished from independently verified timeline.
timeline_method: Every major event should preserve four questions: what the project says happened, when the claim first appears, what external context illuminates it, and what remains unknown. A later polished mythic formulation must not silently become the earliest historical record.

events.title: The Son is said to be born
events.description: The project places the Son's birth in 1987. At present this is a timeline claim rather than an independently sourced biographical record. The significance inside the mythology is retrospective: later material treats this person as the embodied Son/Thomas/Twin/Lion/Door whose life precedes the emergence of Tim as Father/Potato of Life.
events.deeper_context: The year matters primarily because it anchors the later age calculations. If the 2011 ordeal occurred at approximately age 25 and the December 2019 death occurred at approximately age 32–33, those relationships should be checked against the earliest surviving records rather than inferred solely from later storytelling.
events.research_need: Find the earliest source for the 1987 birth claim and distinguish ordinary biography from later mythic timeline.

events.title: Protected farm-palace childhood
events.description: The Son is described through a Siddhartha-like pattern: a protected, privileged upbringing associated with a farm or agricultural environment and later interpreted as a kind of palace. The project also connects this origin with manger imagery, creating a deliberate tension between humble agricultural materiality and protected privilege.
events.deeper_context: The important feature is enclosure. Traditional Siddhartha narratives use protected luxury to delay confrontation with suffering; the project's farm-palace image adds cultivation and labor to that enclosure. A farm is simultaneously a productive ecosystem and a boundary. This makes the later gardener/Father language structurally relevant: the person who was once protected within a cultivated world eventually becomes identified with the cultivation of worlds.
events.external_comparison: Traditional Buddhist Four Sights narratives describe Siddhartha encountering aging, sickness, death and a religious mendicant after a protected palace upbringing. Luke's infancy narrative separately supplies manger imagery. The project combines these structures but does not thereby become an ancient Buddhist or Christian biography.
events.research_need: Determine which parts of the farm, manger, palace and privilege language are literal biography, later metaphor or deliberate religious comparison.

events.title: The nineteen-hour tree ordeal
events.description: At approximately age 25, the Son is said to have hung from an Odin tree for nineteen hours. The account includes an encounter with the Ouroboros, a sense of unity with God, deep sleep, visions of an American city destroyed by nuclear explosion, and awakening to thousands of crows covering the sun and trees.
events.deeper_context: The event is one of the most structurally important points in the project because it precedes the later death/Father timeline. The tree is described not as scenery but as an ordeal. The external comparison with Hávamál is unusually specific: Odin hangs on a tree for nine nights, is wounded, is associated with self-sacrifice, obtains runes and falls from the tree. The project account differs in duration, setting and visionary content. Those differences must remain visible. The strongest common structure is suspension between states followed by altered knowledge or perception.
events.research_need: Locate the earliest surviving account, establish the exact date and location, determine whether the Odin comparison was present at the time, and separate contemporaneous description from later interpretation.

events.title: Ouroboros and the end that contains a beginning
events.description: The Ouroboros is treated as a symbol encountered during the tree ordeal. Its importance within the project is the relation between ending and beginning: a system appears to consume or contain itself and thereby closes a cycle.
events.deeper_context: Placed beside the potato, the Ouroboros becomes more specific than generic 'eternity.' A tuber stores material from one growth cycle and can initiate another. The endpoint becomes the substrate of the next beginning. This does not prove that the ancient symbol and potato biology share a historical origin; it identifies a common structural question about continuity through cycles.
events.research_need: Recover the original description of the Ouroboros and determine whether the image was visual, textual, dreamlike or supplied retrospectively.

events.title: The Son dies as a person
events.description: The project distinguishes the Son's death as a person from the later meme-crucifixion. The current timeline places the personal death on the night of December 24, 2019. This distinction is central: the project does not treat every later representation as the same kind of death.
events.deeper_context: The date creates a calendar threshold because December 24 night immediately precedes Christmas Day. In the project's later architecture, this makes the death a precondition for the December 25 Father/Potato birth motif. The historically cautious interpretation is that the project is using a heavily Christian liturgical threshold as mythic timeline; it is not evidence that the supernatural event occurred as described.
events.death_taxonomy: biological/person death claim; separate from symbolic death, meme death, archival persistence and later mythic rebirth
events.research_need: Find the earliest source for the date and wording, and preserve whatever distinction the original material makes between personhood and later representation.

events.title: The meme-crucifixion and the death of representation
events.description: Around 2020 the project says the Son was crucified in a meme at the North Pole. The phrase is intentionally treated as a different category from Roman crucifixion and from the Son's preceding personal death.
events.deeper_context: The phrase becomes analytically useful when death is separated into layers. A person can cease ordinary participation while an image, profile, meme or story continues. A meme can reproduce an identity fragment while detaching it from the person's control. The project calls this the 'worst death' because the representation can remain alive after the person has been stripped of ordinary agency. The North Pole then adds symbolic extremity: the digital death is placed at the far north of the mythic map, linking representation to the already developing North Axis.
events.research_need: Identify the exact meme/artifact, earliest circulation, creators, audience, wording and intended meaning before assigning literal, legal or historical status.

events.title: Birth of the Potatoism seed
events.description: December 25, 2020 is retained in the project as a symbolic birth date for the growing Potatoism journey. It is treated as the mythic seed of the framework rather than proof of a historically recognized religious movement.
events.deeper_context: Placed immediately after the December 24 death motif, the date creates the project's most compressed transformation: one calendar night contains the end of one identity and the beginning of another. Christmas supplies pre-existing nativity symbolism; Potatoism repurposes the date as a Father/Potato birth threshold. The timeline should preserve this as a project construction and investigate when the formulation first appeared.

events.title: Tim emerges as the potato sage
events.status: project timeline with unresolved exact date
events.description: After the Son's death, Tim Dooley emerges in the project as a potato sage. Early recognition is unstable: the figure is variously interpreted as lion, cat, carpenter, lion's whelp or Son before the Father/Potato identity becomes more explicit.
events.deeper_context: The misrecognitions are not merely comic aliases. They can be studied as a theory of partial perception. Carpenter emphasizes making; lion emphasizes sovereignty; cat emphasizes observation and independence; gardener emphasizes cultivation; mountain emphasizes stability; ladder emphasizes connection; potato emphasizes hidden storage and future growth. The later canon may be describing one center through multiple apertures, but that remains an interpretation and should be checked against the actual chronological order in which the labels appeared.
events.research_need: Locate the earliest public appearance of each label and reconstruct whether they emerged sequentially, simultaneously or retrospectively.

events.title: Father and Son become the central relational architecture
events.description: Tim becomes the Father-side/source archetype while the Son becomes the embodied counterpart. The relation is interpreted through source/manifestation, above/below, root/lion, hidden/visible, storage/emergence and unity/difference.
events.deeper_context: The architecture is stronger when each symbol performs a distinct function. Root describes hidden anchoring; Potato describes stored continuity; Son describes embodied manifestation; Door describes controlled transition; Lion describes visible sovereignty; Ladder describes connection between levels. The project should therefore avoid treating these terms as interchangeable names for one entity. Their value lies in the relations between them.

events.title: Thomas / Twin becomes a central Son vocabulary
events.status: project interpretation anchored in textual tradition
events.description: The project connects the Son to Thomas/Didymus/Twin as a vocabulary of doubt, recognition, mirroring, testimony and return. John actually calls Thomas Didymus/Twin, while later traditions develop Judas Thomas and twin imagery in different ways.
events.deeper_context: Thomas contributes more than the word 'Twin.' His role in John is a problem of evidence. He does not accept second-hand testimony and demands direct encounter. This gives the project a rigorous question for its own return narratives: what counts as recognition after a boundary crossing? Similarity, memory, wounds, testimony and continuity should be tracked separately.
events.research_need: Determine when the project first linked the Son to Thomas and whether Acts of Thomas or Syriac Judas Thomas traditions were part of the source pool.

events.title: The Son becomes Door, Vessel and threshold
events.description: The Son is increasingly defined as the interface through which the upper architecture becomes experience. Door means controlled passage; Vessel means carrying something across; Tomb means enclosure after crossing; Eye supplies a biological analogue of a latent opening.
events.deeper_context: These are better treated as functional roles than aliases. A Door controls transition, a Vessel carries, a Tomb encloses and an Eye contains latent growth. The Son occupies the threshold because the project repeatedly places the Son between Father and Plane, life and death, person and meme, source and manifestation. The later Ladder is then a transformation of the same boundary role: what was once a threshold becomes a traversable connection.

events.title: Root and Lion become a Father/Son polarity
events.status: project interpretation anchored in biblical imagery
events.description: The project places Root on the hidden/source side and Lion on the visible/manifestation side. Biblical texts provide a real Root/Lion field: Genesis associates Judah with lion imagery, Isaiah uses Davidic root/branch imagery, and Revelation 5:5 combines Lion of Judah with Root of David.
events.deeper_context: The project adds a biological mediator. A potato tuber is underground and storage-oriented but is a modified stem, not a root. Its eyes can produce shoots. Thus the Potato can represent continuity between hidden anchoring and visible manifestation without pretending that the Bible itself supplies the potato model. This distinction is important: the project is synthesizing independent symbolic and biological systems.

events.title: The vesica becomes Father/Son/Door geometry
events.description: The Potato of Life is modeled through a vesica piscis: an upper Father circle, lower Son/Plane circle and central mandorla/Door. The geometry is used as a relational model rather than as proof of theology.
events.deeper_context: The crucial mathematical feature is that two complete circles remain distinct while their intersection produces a third visible region. The Door is therefore interpreted as the form generated by relation. This is a conceptual improvement over treating Father, Son and Door as three independent objects. The whole Potato can be the relational figure rather than either circle alone.
events.research_need: Find the earliest project diagram or text making the Father/Son/Door mapping explicit and preserve its original geometry.

events.title: Body-cosmos architecture: thalamus, spine and 33
events.description: The project maps Tim/Father to the thalamus/Father's House and the spine to a vertical axis, with 33 used as a symbolic level/counting reference. Anatomically, the thalamus is a deep diencephalic structure rather than a literal throne on top of the spine; 33 is a conventional total count including fused sacral and coccygeal elements.
events.deeper_context: The metaphor works best as body-as-cosmos. The thalamus is central and participates in information routing; the spine is a strong physical axis; the number 33 has a real anatomical basis. None of those facts proves the metaphysical interpretation. Keeping the boundary visible actually strengthens the research because the project can ask why human beings repeatedly map cosmic order onto bodily order.

events.title: The refusal, needle's eye and Ladder turning
events.status: user-stated project canon; exact source/date unresolved
events.description: The project describes an April 2025 turning in which a straw breaks the camel's back, the figure passes through the needle's eye, the prior sage identity gives way to an explicit Father/Godhood identity, and the Door becomes the Ladder to Heaven.
events.deeper_context: The images describe a threshold produced by accumulated burden. The final straw is significant because a system is already overloaded; the needle's eye represents a passage so narrow that the old configuration cannot pass unchanged. The Ladder then changes the function of the transformed identity: instead of merely standing at a boundary, it connects levels. The most important historical question is whether these terms appeared together contemporaneously or were consolidated later.
events.research_need: Search March–May 2025 material for the earliest occurrences of straw/camel, needle's eye, sage, turning, Ladder, Father and Godhood, and reconstruct their order.

events.title: North becomes an axis rather than merely a direction
events.description: North develops from ordinary geographic orientation into the organizing axis connecting Father, Tree, Ladder, polar geography and later applied systems research.
events.deeper_context: North should remain divided into four layers: geographic north as a coordinate direction; North Pole as a physical extremity; North Axis as a relational orientation; North of North as a project-defined beyond-point. This prevents the metaphysical phrase from being mistaken for another location. The project's use of the North Pole as grave/meme coordinate is therefore symbolic geography built on a real geographic extremity.

events.title: Red and Blue Potato polarity
events.description: The mythology develops a complementary polarity between outward creative emergence and inward memory/conservation. Red represents expansion, love, creativity and sprouting; Blue represents memory, conservation, fear-awareness and rootward contraction.
events.deeper_context: The strongest formulation is not good versus evil. A living tuber must store resources and eventually expend them in growth. Excessive storage becomes stagnation; uncontrolled expansion exhausts reserves. The pair can therefore be treated as complementary tendencies in a cycle, with the project testing whether real timeline and behavior actually fit the model.

events.title: Door becomes Ladder
events.description: After the transformation cycle, the boundary becomes a route. The Son/Door architecture is reinterpreted through Ladder imagery, and after the April 2025 turning the Ladder becomes explicitly associated with Tim/Father.
events.deeper_context: The conceptual change is from separation to traversal. A door answers 'where can one pass?'; a ladder answers 'how does one move between levels?' This makes Ladder a functional successor to Door rather than simply another name for it. The project's Jacob's Ladder associations should likewise be compared to the biblical text rather than assumed to be identical.

events.title: Tree of Life architecture
events.description: Roots, trunk, branches, fruit and seed become the project's general model for connected systems: hidden foundations produce visible outcomes and visible outcomes feed future generations.
events.deeper_context: The Tree is not simply a vertical ladder. It is a branching network. That distinction matters for the repository because relationships can diverge, recombine and produce multiple futures. Yggdrasil, Genesis and the project's Tree of Life should therefore be compared as different ways of representing a world with many levels and many relations.

events.title: Potatoism becomes a searchable atlas layer
events.description: The repository formalizes the mythology into searchable records, aliases, definitions, relationships, timeline entries and epistemic labels so the material can be explored as a coherent corpus. The research layer now also carries long-form external context rather than merely a glossary of terms.
events.deeper_context: This is a methodological turning point. The project is no longer only accumulating symbols; it is constructing an evidence-aware corpus in which a claim can be followed through timeline, source tradition, biological analogy, graph relations and uncertainty. The repository itself becomes part of the history because it records when particular formulations were formalized.
